summary: Peter Thomi is an Indologist who studied under Alfred Bloch. He served as the head (Leiter) of the Institut für Indologie Wichtrach (attested 1995).

Peter Zieme is a specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Humboldt University, he held posts at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (1965–2007) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007).

Peter van der Veer is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Groningen and Utrecht. He was a professor at the University of Amsterdam and served as Director of the Max Planck Institute (MMG) from ~2008 to 2021.

Peter von Bohlen (1796–1840) was an Indologist who studied at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin under Bopp, Freytag, Gesenius, and Schlegel. He served as ordinary professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1828.

Peter von Bradke (1853–1897) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu, Tübingen, Jena, Leipzig, and Munich under Meyer, Roth, and Delbrück. He served as an associate professor (ao. Professor) at the University of Giessen (1886–1896).

Peter von Köppen (1793–1864) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv and the University of Tübingen, later serving in the Ministry of State Property (~1837–1860).
Petr Sgall (1926–2019) was a Czech linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University under doctoral supervisor Vincenc Lesný and subsequently held a post there from ~1953 to 1995.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Heinz Bechert. She held research posts at the Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Literatur Mainz and is attested as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society in 2026.

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. Her career includes posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities and as apl. Professorin at the University of Munich.

id: P:Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer
summary: Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer (1829–1873) was an Indologist who completed a Dr.juris at the University of Groningen (1844–1850). He held a research post at the Nationaal Archief in 1865.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist who earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute and studied under masters including Dilgo Khyentse and Tulku Urgyen. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.

Phanit Jetjiravat is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the academic supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn (1933–2016) was a historian and sinologist educated at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and Professor of History and East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard from 1978.

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate from the University of Manchester. He later served as Professor of Religion and Social Theory and Head of Humanities at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).

Philip Anderson (1816–1857) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his B.A. from the University of Cambridge (~1834–1838) and served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Philip Boas Yampolsky (1920–1996) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, he served as Adjunct Associate Professor of Japanese and East Asian Library Director at Columbia (1968–1996).

Philip C. Almond is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Adelaide (1975–1980) and became an Emeritus professor at the University of Queensland, where he held a post from 1982.

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer (~1990–1996). He was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig around 2008.

Philip Deslippe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Connecticut, University of Iowa, and UC Santa Barbara, he has served as a teaching associate at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2020).
